Present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners.
Petitioner no.1 is wife of deceased (who has also expired during pendency of proceedings), petitioner no. 2 to 4 are children of deceased.

As per the claim petition, deceased Mohd. Shafiq along with his nephew Javed met with a roadside accident on 31.03.2014, at about 08:30 a.m., while crossing the road from Welcome Red light, Main road, GT Road, Shahdara, Delhi when suddenly a bus bearing registration no. UK-07PA-2074 which was being driven by the respondent no.1 in a very rash and negligent manner at a high speed came and hit Mohd. Shafiq due to which he received multiple and grievous injuries on various parts of his body.
Thereafter, he was removed to G.T.B. hospital where he was examined and his MLC was prepared vide No.B- 1146/14.
Due to the injuries received, he succumbed to injuries on the next day of the accident.
2. It is further mentioned in the claim petition that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1/driver of Bus bearing registration no.UK-07PA-2074.

Issue No.1 8.

It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of accident having occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
As such, petitioner has to establish occurring of an accident and that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and MACT No.1418/2016 Zubeda Begum Vs. Jitender Sharma & Ors.

PW2 was duly cross examined by respondent no.1 as respondent no.2 however nothing substantive came in cross examination to disbelieve the version given by PW2 rather the plea/defence as taken by respondent no.1 and 2 in their pleadings to the effect that "in fact deceased was trying to cross over the road by jumping over the divider and in that process he fell on the road and died due to his own negligence", has not been MACT No.1418/2016 Zubeda Begum Vs. Moreover evidence of PW2 gets support from the statement given by the same witness to the police which led to registration of FIR No.191/2014.
Respondent no.1/driver of the offending vehicle was apprehended at the spot not only by PW2 but other public persons and was arrested by the police on the same day.

Beside the testimony of PW2, criminal case documents including site plan, mechanical inspection report etc also established that deceased was hit over by the offending bus no.UK-07PA-2074 when he was trying to cross over the road.

There cannot be any automatic contributory negligence attributable to the deceased only for the reason that deceased was trying to cross over the road, firstly because nothing came either in police documents or by way of cross examination that there was any foot over bridge or any zebra crossing nearby.
11. Respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle has been examined as R1W1 and testified all those facts as pleaded in their WS.

However in his cross examination he admitted that on 31.03.2014 he was the driver of the offending vehicle and police reached at the spot of accident and he was arrested after registration of FIR on the same day.
PW R1W1 further admitted that he never filed any complaint regarding his false implication in the criminal case.

12. Thus for the reasons as noted above this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient evidence available on the record to conclude that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.

In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.

The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the MACT Zubeda Begum vs Jitender Sharma on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94516866/

Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

sentences.text: " ( iii

) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
(iv) In case, the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

opennyai_summary.facts: Case of the MACT No.1418/2016 Zubeda Begum Vs. Jitender Sharma & Ors.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of pleadings as come on the record, Ld. Predecessor of this court on 15.12.2016 framed following issues:
1.Whether respondent no. 1 was driving vehicle bearing no. UK-07PA-2074 on 31.03.2014 at 12.30 pm at Red Light ,Welcome, GT Road, Delhi in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against Md. Shafiq who sustained fatal injuries?
OPP. 
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation,if so and for what amount ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of accident having occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
As such, petitioner has to establish occurring of an accident and that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and MACT No.1418/2016 Zubeda Begum Vs. Jitender Sharma & Ors.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others.
There cannot be any automatic contributory negligence attributable to the deceased only for the reason that deceased was trying to cross over the road, firstly because nothing came either in police documents or by way of cross examination that there was any foot over bridge or any zebra crossing nearby.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
Moreover document Ex.PW1/A does not bear any firm number or GST number to authenticate the same.
Nor any document has been placed on record to show that any such firm in the name and style "Khan Garments" is a registered firm.
PW2 has not produced on record any document showing attendance of the deceased in his said firm or the ledger of his said firm to show that any payment was made to the deceased from the accounts of MACT No.1418/2016 Zubeda Begum Vs. Jitender Sharma & Ors.
Thus this Tribunal assesses income of deceased to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in Delhi which at the time of accident was of Rs.8,086/- per month.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v.
MACT No.1418/2016 Zubeda Begum Vs. Jitender Sharma & Ors.
Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case MACT No.1418/2016 Zubeda Begum Vs. Jitender Sharma & Ors. Page 13 titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020,
decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Instant claim petition has been filed by four petitioners i.e. widow and children of deceased.
Since, the deceased was survived by four dependents, one-fourth of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
27.
In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-,

8 18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
Since, the deceased was survived by four legal heirs, therefore, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.2,28,000/-
(48,000 X 4 + 18,000 + 18,000) under this head.
28. Considering the aforementioned factors, the total compensation is calculated as under:
S. No. Head Amount Awarded 1.
Monthly income of deceased (A) Rs.8,086/-
2. Less 1/4th towards personal and living Rs.2,021.50 expenses of the deceased (B)
3.
Monthly loss of dependency (A+B)= C Rs.6,064.50 4.
Annual loss of dependency (Cx12) Rs.72,774/-
6.
Total loss of dependency (Dx12xE=E) Rs.5,09,418/-
7. Compensation for loss of consortium Rs.1,92,000/-
(48,000 X 4) (F)
8.
Compensation for loss of estate (G) Rs.18,000/-
9.
Compensation for funeral expenses (H) Rs.18,000/-
Total compensation (E + F + G + H) Rs.7,37,418/-
29.
Thus, petitioners in this case shall be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,37,418/- only.
INTEREST ON AWARD 30.
Petitioners shall also be entitled to interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
LIABILITY 31.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Page 14 offending vehicle was not insured, therefore the amount of compensation is payable by respondent no.1 and 2 jointly and severally to the petitioners.
This Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.7,37,418/- to the petitioners along with interest @
8% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by respondent no.1 and 2 jointly and severally.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.
The respondent no.1 and 2 are directed to deposit the award amount in A/c no.20780110171912 (IFSC Code UCBA0002078), UCO Bank, Karkardooma, Delhi, of PO MACT, Shahdara, through RTGS/ NEFT, within 30 days from today.
Respondent no.1 and 2 is also directed to give notice regarding deposit of the said amount to the petitioners.
Disbursement and Apportionment of Award Amount 33.
The awarded amount is proportioned as under:
(i) A sum of Rs.24,502/- each is directed to be released into the saving account of petitioners namely Tabassum, Imran Khan and Shakeel and amount of Rs.2,21,304/-
each along with interest on entire awarded amount is directed to be kept in their names with UCO Bank, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi in Motor Accident Claims Annuity Deposit (MACAD) in the form of 60 FDRs (fixed deposit receipts).

The petitioners shall open a saving bank account near the place of their residence.
